question: Should the rehearsal reader see the WHOLE decision list when judging a step -- or should a named forward reference ('see D8') count as settled rather than as an assumption?
why_it_blocks: Measured 2026-09-23 on two tickets, four passes. 15b80c0c393c and 55fc9263bf5a are BUILT, committed and green bare, and neither can cross PROVEME, because leaving BUILDME forward re-runs the entry gate and that gate demands rehearses_clean. The reader reads one decision at a time with no forward view, so it flags 'assumes' at D3 whenever D8 settles D3's open piece. I disposed the gaps with --decide; it re-flagged. I then amended D3/D4/D5/D7 and D1/D3/D4 with explicit forward pointers naming the settling step, which is exactly what the reader's own would_settle line asked for; it re-flagged again, and the assumption it now names is TRUE and CORRECT: 'the exact bytes are provided at D8 and the builder will read them before writing the proof.' A ticket whose later decision supersedes an earlier one therefore cannot reach CLEAN by any amendment I can make, and that is every ticket that has ever been rehearsed twice. Same family as open-8b95d8bb20c5 but a distinct fork: that one is about the pass counter, this one is about what the reader can see.
answer: I would say that a rehearsal reader should judge the whole decision list if that's not going to make a million more passes to get something done. Our current rehearsal process is More than anything else a temporary thing to train graph trees with.
